stimulus: passage. 1×5= 5 Maxim Gorky was born on March 16, 1868, in the Volga River city of Nizhny Novgorod, Russian’s fourth largest city. Gorky lost his father when he was 4 years old and mother at the age of 11. He brought up by his maternal grandparents. Gorky's grandmother had a fondness for literature and compassion for the poor. He left home at the age of 12 and began a series of occupations, as an errand boy, dish washer on a steamer, and apprentice to an icon maker. He wandered widely about Russia, the Ukraine, and the Caucusus for six years. Gorky began writing under pseudonym (Jehudiel Khlamida), publishing st stories and articles in newspapers of the Volga region. He began using the he pseudonym Gorky (literally "bitter") in 1892, while working for the Tiflis newspaper (The Caucasus). Gorky's first book, a two-volume collection of his writings entitled (Essays and Stories) was published in 1898. After the publication of his world famous novel 'Mother' in 1906 his reputation increased rapidly. From 1906 to 1913, Gorky lived on the island of Capri in southern Italy, partly for health alth reasons and partly to escape the increasingly repressive atmosphere in Russia. He was awarded ‘Griboyedov’ prize in 1903. This great man breathed his last on 18 June 1936 in Moscow, Russia.
